findings.title: Changelog entries from earlier commits state as general what later entries on the branch changed
findings.scenario: Assemble [Unreleased] with /home/user/polish-tools/mkchangelog.py and read it as one text. (1) caceef3 (Fixed): "Each file's preview now starts at its top" stands beside 7228253 (Added) "The preview of a contents search result opens at the matching line" and 52e7de4 "text stays where you were reading it". (2) 323f173 (Changed): "A search that comes back runs again with the kind and the Nushell filter chosen now, in relevance order." stands beside 60df179 "Back and Forward return to a Smart Folder's search with its kind and filter." (3) da6a5b9 (Fixed) calls `basic.txt` for `music` a "near miss with typos"; 5624239 (Changed) defines a near miss as one typo in one place (two for 8+ letters), under which `basic.txt` (two wrong letters in a 5-letter word) is exactly what is no longer listed. (4) 323f173 says going elsewhere by "the sidebar" keeps the search in the history; a click on a Smart Folder that searches This Computer (or whose folder is gone) replaces the search instead, as the record of back-forward-restore-search itself says ("Neither is one replaced where it stands: ... a Smart Folder with no folder"); docs/manual.md:337 has the same blanket "a click in the sidebar". (2) "A search that comes back runs again with the kind and the Nushell filter chosen now, in relevance order; a Smart Folder's search comes back with its own kind and filter." (3) "Matches that fff-search only made by leaving letters out then stayed in the list beside the real matches, so `music` also listed `basic.txt`." (4) changelog and manual: "...a folder or place clicked in the sidebar or the path bar..." and add to manual.md:337 "Opening a Smart Folder that searches This Computer takes the search's place, as typing other words does."

findings.title: Two UI tests check "Indexing…" only if a real scan thread loses a race, and pass in silence otherwise
findings.scenario: indexing_stays_while_the_search_is_tried_again has every assertion inside `if ui.names().is_empty() { ... }`; a_folder_whose_index_is_still_being_built_doesnt_say_no_results has its "Indexing…" assertion in the same kind of branch. The branch runs only when fff-search's scan of the 300-file folder (a real thread started by the first search) is still going when the search reads the index. When the scan wins, or once anything prepares that index earlier (the queued adhoc-index work would), the first test asserts nothing and still prints ok; nothing is printed either way. The reviewer's record notes it ("otherwise it passes without checking") but it is not in final-pass-notes.md and nothing in the test says so.
findings.code_path: tests/controls.rs:2141-2172 (all asserts under the `if` at :2158) ; tests/controls.rs:2119-2121 ; the race: src/finder/mod.rs:2233-2238 (engine.search on the background executor) -> crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:896-897 (`indexing = indexes.iter().any(|r| r.scanning())` read right after indexes_for starts the scan on fff-search's own thread).
findings.tests_gap: These are the tests. They guard bc834b7's rule that a retried search over a half-built index shows no placeholders; a regression there is caught only on runs where the race goes the usual way, and a change that makes the index ready first removes the guard without a failure.
findings.fix: Make the precondition deterministic or loud: retry with a fresh outside folder until the first answer comes from a scanning index (bounded, then panic "never caught the index being built"), or at least `else { panic!/eprintln }` so a run that checked nothing says so.
findings.test_idea: Add `engine.prepare(Some(outside.dir.as_path()), 20 s)` before `ui.click("search")` in indexing_stays_while_the_search_is_tried_again: it still passes though no line after the `if` ran. With an `else { panic!("nothing was checked") }` it fails.

findings.title: New nu tests run whatever `nu` the machine has, and their last assertions vanish without one
findings.scenario: The harness opens windows with no `nu` so that "tests never depend on what is installed" (tests/common/mod.rs:149-151). settings_nu_choice clicks Find Automatically, which calls find_nu(None) over PATH and the usual install folders, puts that program in AppState and has every browser run it on the starter actions.nu; the test then asserts `user_actions_error() == None`. On a machine whose `nu` is older than the starters need (the manual asks for 0.116) or is a broken stub on PATH, the test fails for a reason outside the tree. In the other direction, what_waited_for_a_nu_runs_with_the_one_chosen_in_settings and quick_look_explores_with_a_nu_chosen_while_it_is_open wrap their final assertions in `if find_nu(None).is_some() { ... }` with no else and no message, so without nu the part that proves a real nu is picked up again is skipped and the test still reads ok (the other nu tests at least eprintln a skip line, which cargo hides for passing tests).
findings.code_path: tests/controls.rs:3157-3166 (click nu-auto, then assert no actions error with the found nu) -> src/finder/mod.rs:3671-3676 (set_nu_path -> look_for_nu -> nushell::find_nu) -> :3681-3686 nu_changed -> :3724-3735 load_user_actions -> user_actions::discover(&nu, ..) runs the program ; tests/controls.rs:3236-3246 and tests/finder.rs:2144-2151 (asserts only inside `if find_nu(None).is_some()`).
findings.tests_gap: The suite has only been run in this container, where nu 0.116.0 is installed, so neither direction has shown.
findings.fix: Have the tests choose the file to find: point the lookup at a stand-in script (as tests/nu_module.rs:66 does) through PATH set for the test or a test seam in find_nu, and replace the bare `if ... is_some()` blocks with the `let Some(nu) = ... else { eprintln!("nu not installed; skipping"); return }` form used elsewhere, split into a test of their own.
findings.test_idea: Run tests/controls.rs settings_nu_choice with PATH led by a folder holding an executable `nu` that exits 1: it fails at the `user_actions_error` assertion although nothing in fffinder is wrong.

findings.title: results_follow_what_a_watched_index_reports sleeps on the real clock and needs a real file watcher
findings.scenario: The test opens the engine with watch: true and then polls with std::thread::sleep(50 ms) up to 200 times (10 s) per step for fff-search's watcher to start, to report a new file, a removed one, and a new one for Recents. On a loaded machine (other cargo builds, as here), or where no inotify watch or instance is left (the manual's own caveat about fs.inotify limits), a step runs out and the test fails with "the window didn't have the index report its changes" or a list of names; the first loop also depends on the window's 30 s FOLLOW_TRIES budget not being used up by the fake clock (100 ms per turn, so 20 s). It is the only UI test tied to wall time; every other live-results test injects reports with report_change.
findings.code_path: tests/finder.rs:987-1046 (pause at :997, loops at :1003, :1021, :1029, :1040) ; src/finder/mod.rs:2463-2476 and :4183 (FOLLOW_TRIES = 75 tries, 400 ms apart) ; crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:659-678 (follow_changes waits for fff-search's watcher).
findings.tests_gap: It is the test; its timing margins were only tried on this machine.
findings.fix: Keep it out of the default run (a named `#[ignore]` with a line in the manual's Tests section, run in CI by name), or wait on engine.follow_changes() == true and on engine.changes() moving with a longer bound instead of fixed 10 s windows.
findings.test_idea: Run it with `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` exhausted, or under `stress --cpu` for the duration: it fails with no change to the code.

findings.title: Six more test-only entry points are compiled into the app, one of which writes fake watcher reports into the engine
findings.scenario: The branch adds `pub fn ..._for_test` methods that are not behind cfg(test) or a feature, because tests/*.rs are separate crates: Engine::report_change_for_test (counts a made-up Created/Removed/Renamed/Modified event and marks the index as reporting), Finder::search_in_flight_for_test, search_abort_for_test (hands out the live abort flag of the running search), preview_text_for_test, preview_match_for_test, smart_is_active_for_test. They ship in the binary and are callable by any code in the workspace (the server, examples); report_change_for_test panics with "a file in a search location" for a path outside every root. Upstream already had ten such accessors, so this follows the house pattern; it is listed because the lens asks for it.
findings.code_path: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:780-814 ; src/finder/mod.rs:1015-1025 ; src/finder/preview.rs:406-428 ; src/finder/sidebar.rs:904 ; used from tests/common/mod.rs:302-304 and tests/finder.rs.

notes:
All ten findings hold as facts against the snapshot at 7e8df53, and none is worse than severity 2. None is a fault in how the app behaves: they are changelog, manual and dialog wording, and the make-up of tests.

- **Not on record (five):** the two changelog findings, the Save dialog's "Kept up to date." for a contents search, the "every word must match" strings, and the Search Syntax footer.
- **Already on record as known or deliberate (five):** the two "Indexing…" tests, the nu tests, the real-watcher test, the F5 rows with the Mac-only test, and the test hooks. I found none of them worse than recorded.

Where the finder was imprecise:
- **Changelog contradictions:** the pairing with 52e7de4 is not a contradiction, and the manual already carries the Smart Folder exception.
- **Never-shipped faults:** `music` listing `basic.txt` did ship in v0.5.1; only the Allow typos clause is about unreleased behaviour.
- **Save dialog:** the line is upstream's, from before the branch, where it meant "searched again when opened".
- **nu tests:** the quoted harness comment is about terminals, and upstream's own tests already run the machine's nu and check less without one.
- **F5:** the Mac's key table is unit-tested on every system, CI runs macOS, and the manual rows are upstream's.
- **Footer:** "Return searches now" is still true during the 50 ms pause; what is stale is the split between Return and Down Arrow.

I ran no build and no test. Everything is from git, grep and reading, plus a 20-line Python copy of `near_miss` to check `music` against `basic.txt`. I assembled the changelog paragraphs from the snapshot's own commits instead of running mkchangelog.py, which reads /home/user/fffinder. My scratch folder is deleted and the snapshot is unchanged.

The relayed request ("Just reset the limit") names nothing this step could act on. I changed no limit and no setting.

findings.title: A file saved the usual way keeps its old size, date and preview in Recents (when it stays where it was) and in name-search results: the reread's answer is compared by path only and dropped
findings.scenario: 1. Recents (Cmd+Shift+F), Preview Pane on (Cmd+Shift+P). The newest file, say notes.txt, is first: select it. 2. Save notes.txt again from an editor that writes a draft and renames it over the file (most do). It is still the newest, so it stays first. 3. Wait. What happens: the row keeps the old Date Modified and Size and the pane (Quick Look and the gallery too) keeps the old text, for good. The index reported the rename, the window read Recents again and the answer held the new size and date, but `fresh` only asks whether the paths differ, so the answer is thrown away, `listing` is not replaced and `selection_changed` is never reached. The same save seen in the file's own folder updates row and preview within two seconds. In the results of a search by name it is the same for any listed file: a file the search already lists is no news to `changes_for`, and when a rerun does happen (the draft's name had the words) `Stale::shows_in` compares paths, so `results` keeps the old entries. What should happen: the row shows the new size and date and the preview is read again, as docs/manual.md:424 says ("...when a search runs again, or when Recents is read again. Most programs save a file under another name that then takes the file's ... so the preview follows within a couple of seconds") and as both changes' changelog entries say. Already recorded, and not what this is about: files written over in place (final-pass-notes lines 47 and 71, manual line 139 "with the size and date it showed"). Not recorded: the ordinary save by rename, and that Recents reads the newer rows and drops them.
findings.code_path: src/finder/mod.rs:1647-1670 (Recents look: a rename is news, so `reload_recents` runs) -> mod.rs:1675-1699 (`fresh` = the paths differ, 1685-1689; `listing` replaced and `selection_changed` called only `if fresh`, 1691-1696). Name search: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:762-776 (a file that came matters only when `!lists(now)`) and src/finder/mod.rs:2273-2284 (`fresh` from `Stale::shows_in`; `if !fresh { return retry; }` before `results` is written) with mod.rs:356-369 (`shows_in` compares paths). engine.rs:1316-1325 (`recents` hands back the index's size and date). src/finder/preview.rs:329-331 and 338-348 (the stamp is the row's entry, so a row that isn't replaced never asks again).
findings.tests_gap: tests/finder.rs:1164-1188 (recents_previews_a_file_as_it_was_last_written) writes to the second file so that it moves first, which changes the order and so counts as fresh. tests/finder.rs:1126-1136 pins "stays first, so Recents isn't read again" and looks at names only. No test saves a listed file that keeps its place and then looks at its row or its preview, in Recents or in a search.
findings.fix: In `reload_recents`, also take the answer when the paths are the same in the same order but some entry's (modified, size) differs: replace `listing`, `rebuild_rows`, `selection_changed`, and count it as fresh (the order is the same, so nothing reshuffles). In the quiet search's answer, when it is not fresh but `paths_of(&this.results).eq(paths_of(&rows))`, take `rows` and call `selection_changed` instead of returning.
findings.test_idea: tests/finder.rs: Recents with Roadmap.md the newest and selected, Preview Pane on. Write new text to a draft and rename it over Roadmap.md, `ui.reindex()`, `ui.report_change(Some(&draft), Some(&roadmap))` (a rename), `ui.look_for_changes(2)`. Assert `preview_text_for_test(&roadmap)` is the new text and the row's size label is the new one. Today both are the old ones. The same with a search for `roadmap` in place of Recents.

findings.title: A Nushell filter is run again only when the list of paths changes: saved files, folder sizes that arrive later, Refresh and Return leave its old answer in force
findings.scenario: Needs nu. A folder sorted by name with a.log (5 KB) and b.log (50 KB). Filter bar: `size > 10kb`; b.log shows. Another program saves a.log at 80 KB (draft renamed over it). After the two-second look the folder is read again and the rows have the new sizes, but a.log stays hidden. Save b.log at 1 KB the same way: it stays listed, showing 1 KB under `size > 10kb`, and the status bar goes on counting it as passing. Cmd+R changes nothing, and neither does Return in the filter field (`set_filter` returns when the text is the same); only editing the filter's text runs it again. With one file in the folder, "No Items Pass the Filter. 1 item is hidden by the filter." stays up after the file has grown past the limit. Second case, by reading: with folder sizes on, the first run after opening a folder judges the folders before `load_folder_stats` has filled their sizes in; when the sizes arrive the rows show them and the filter is not run again, so `size > 100mb` never lists a big folder in a folder opened with the filter on. What should happen: the filter runs again when what it is given for a row (size, date) changed, and at the least on Refresh. Origin: the path-only comparison is upstream's (66c919b had the same `apply_filter_to`); the branch added the message that states the count and the promise that rows and previews follow saved files, which the filter beside them now contradicts.
findings.code_path: src/finder/filter.rs:130-138 (`filter_source` is the ordered list of paths; a run starts only when it differs, otherwise `filter_keep` is applied as it is). filter.rs:83-100 (`set_filter` returns for the same text; it and src/finder/mod.rs:3699-3705 `nu_changed` are the only places that forget the answer). mod.rs:1757-1765 (`refresh` resets nothing of the filter). mod.rs:1835-1836 (`rebuild_rows` -> `apply_filter_to`). src/nushell.rs:69-84 (the filter is given each row's size and modified). src/finder/list.rs:153-156 and 177-183 (folder sizes are filled in later, then `rebuild_rows` with the same paths). mod.rs:4820-4834 and src/finder/bars.rs:353-366 (the message and the status count go by the old answer).
findings.tests_gap: The filter tests change the filter's text or the set of rows. None changes a row's size or date while a filter is on, and none presses Refresh under a filter. what_waited_for_a_nu_runs_with_the_one_chosen_in_settings covers only a change of `nu`.
findings.fix: Keep in `filter_source` what the filter is given for each row, (path, size, modified), and compare that in `apply_filter_to`; and set `filter_source = None` in `refresh`.
findings.test_idea: Where nu is installed (return early otherwise, as the other filter tests do): a fixture folder with small.txt of 1 byte, `set_filter("size > 10b")`, assert small.txt is not listed. Write 100 bytes to a draft and rename it over small.txt, `ui.look_for_changes(1)`, assert small.txt is listed. Fails today. A second block: write over a file in place, `ui.press(&cmd("r"))`, same assertion.

findings.title: Quick Look's window holds its browser strongly, so closing the tab or the window neither closes Quick Look nor stops that browser's background work
findings.scenario: Two tabs. Select a file in the first, press Space: Quick Look opens in its own window. In the browser, click the first tab's close button (or Move Tab to New Window, or close the whole window). What happens, by reading: Quick Look stays open on the file and its arrow keys go on stepping through the items of a tab that no longer exists. The closed tab's browser is never dropped: its two-second look goes on (folders, the index look, quiet search reruns, Recents), a contents search it was running is not told to stop, and it still answers a change of `nu` by starting `nu`. On Linux and Windows the app does not quit after the last browser window is closed, because Quick Look's window is still there. What should happen: Quick Look closes with its browser, as docs/manual.md:444 says ("closes with its browser") and as quick_look.rs:43-44 intends. Origin: upstream's code; this branch made a closed tab's survival cost more (the index look in every tab, `AbortOnDrop`, the AppState observer).
findings.code_path: src/finder/quick_look.rs:142-148: `self.finder.upgrade()` and three `.on_action(text_size_handler(&finder, ..))`; src/finder/preview.rs:706-712: `text_size_handler` clones the `Entity<Finder>` into the closure. quick_look.rs:161-167 and 194-197 hand the same strong entity to `preview_area`, `text_size_buttons` and `mode_buttons`, whose click closures keep it too. Those closures live in the window's rendered frame (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/window.rs:1045-1051, `mouse_listeners` and `dispatch_tree`), and a redraw upgrades the weak handle again because the frame still holds the entity. So the browser is never released while the window is open, and `cx.observe_release_in(finder, .. window.remove_window())` (quick_look.rs:44) cannot fire. Nothing else closes it: src/workspace.rs:215-236 (`close_tab` only drops the tab's entity), workspace.rs:256-277, src/finder/mod.rs:2575-2580 (`close_window` only removes the browser's window). What leans on the drop: mod.rs:1743-1755 (`watch_folder` ends only when the entity is gone), mod.rs:312-329 (`AbortOnDrop`: "when its tab closes"), mod.rs:786 (the AppState observer).
findings.tests_gap: No test closes a tab or a browser window while Quick Look is open. The tests close Quick Look's own window (tests/common/mod.rs:378-386) or look at a tab after Quick Look has closed (tests/settings.rs:95).
findings.fix: Close it explicitly: a `Finder::close_quick_look(cx)` doing what the first branch of `toggle_quick_look_window` does, called from `Workspace::close_tab`, from `toggle_split` when the pane goes, and for every tab from the Workspace's `cx.on_release` (workspace.rs:71). The other way is to give Quick Look's closures a `WeakEntity<Finder>`.
findings.test_idea: tests/controls.rs: open a second tab, select a file in the first, press Space, keep `quick_look_window()` and a `WeakEntity` of the first tab's browser. Close the first tab through `Workspace::close_tab`, settle. Assert that `cx.update_window(handle, ..)` is an error (the window is gone) and that the weak handle no longer upgrades. Both fail today.

findings.title: Left to the parent folder in the list, and Select All, change the shown item without asking for its preview: the Preview Pane and Quick Look show a spinner until something else asks
findings.scenario: List view, Preview Pane on. Open a folder in place with its triangle (which doesn't select it), click a file inside it, press Left. The folder is selected and the pane shows its card with a spinner where the icon and "N items" belong. It stays until another item is selected or the window's folder is read again. With Quick Look open on the file, Left in the browser leaves Quick Look on the same spinner. Also: a folder with one file and nothing selected, Cmd+A: the pane shows the file's card with a spinner. What should happen: the preview is asked for whenever the item that shows changes. Origin: both paths are upstream's; stale-previews-and-cancel fixed the same spinner after Refresh and a change of appearance and left these two.
findings.code_path: src/finder/mod.rs:2823-2825 (`move_selection` returns when `tree_key` took the key, before `selection_changed` at 2844). src/finder/list.rs:279-287 (`tree_key` selects the parent and only notifies). mod.rs:2993-2996 (`select_all` has no `selection_changed`; src/model.rs:484-491 puts the cursor on row 0). mod.rs:2742-2754 (`selection_changed` is the only asker outside the gallery). src/finder/preview.rs:389-394 and 991-996 (`preview_of` gives Loading, which draws the spinner). src/finder/preview_pane.rs:62-92.
findings.tests_gap: the_preview_pane_follows_the_selection (tests/basics.rs:1802-1829) selects with clicks. The tree's Left is tested for the selection only. No test looks at the preview after Left or after Cmd+A.
findings.fix: Call `self.selection_changed(cx)` after `self.selection.select_only(up)` in `tree_key`, and at the end of `select_all`.
findings.test_idea: tests/basics.rs: list view, pane on, open Projects in place without selecting it, click the item inside, press Left. Assert `has_preview_for_test(&fx.path("Projects"))`. False today.

The outcome is real, and nothing guards against it. It is recorded as known and left, and tests pin it. done/live-search-results.json: behaviour_changes "While it is first, further writes read nothing and its row keeps the size and date it showed"; left_out "Rows of files changed in place keep their old size and date until the list is next replaced ... That includes a file that stays first in Recents"; notes "`reload_recents` shows a list only when its paths or their order differ" and "a quiet rerun compares which paths are listed, not their sizes or dates ... a preview cache stamped from the row won't see a new stamp from it". done/stale-previews-and-cancel.json, Found, not fixed: "In the results of a search by name a file changed in place keeps the index's size and date, so its preview isn't read again until the search's rows change". final-pass-notes.md lines 47 and 71. docs/manual.md:139 says of Recents "stays there however often it's written to, with the size and date it showed". tests/finder.rs:1126-1133 pins "stays first, so Recents isn't read again"; engine.rs:3662 pins "a file the search lists already is nothing new to it". So the finder's "not recorded: that Recents reads the newer rows and drops them" is wrong: it is in the done record's notes. The finder's quote of manual.md:424 also leaves out "which changes the folder": that sentence promises the couple of seconds for folders only.

What the records do not say in so many words: in these two lists a save by rename is treated no differently from a write in place. "Changed in place" in final-pass-notes 47 and 71 therefore understates the limit: any save of a file that stays listed (name search) or stays first (Recents) leaves its row and preview as they were.
verdicts.corrected_scenario: The row and the preview stay as they were until Recents next comes out as another list, the search's rows change, or Cmd+R; not for good. How it happens depends on what the watcher reports. A draft made and renamed within one batch reaches the app as `Modified` of the target: fff-notify-debouncer-full-0.9.4 src/lib.rs:469-484 rewrites the draft's events to the target path and adds no rename event "unless the file was just created", and fff-search-0.11.0 src/watcher/background_watcher.rs:629-632 gives `None if existed => (WatchEventKind::Modified, None)`. Then for the first file in Recents `only_written_since` names it and nothing is read at all (mod.rs:1659-1664: `if news || written.as_deref() != first { fell_behind }`), which is the documented skip, and a name search hears nothing (Modified counts only in `recent`, engine.rs:396-409). Recents is read and its answer dropped, as the finder describes, only when the save arrives as Renamed or Created: a draft that outlived a batch, or an editor that moves the old file aside first. A listed file never makes a name search run again in either case. The finder's fix (take the answer when stamps differ) reaches only the read-and-dropped case, not the usual quick save.

verdicts.corrected_scenario: As the finder says, with these limits. The saved-file and Refresh cases need the rows' paths and order to stay the same: a sort by name does that, while Sort By Size (or by date for a date filter) moves the changed row and the filter runs again. A visible draft that a 2-second look happens to catch in the folder also makes it run again. The folder case exactly: type `size > 100mb` in a folder whose sizes have loaded and its big folders are listed; open another folder with the filter still on and that folder's big folders are not listed, until the folder gains or loses an item (the reread then finds the stats still in the map and the paths changed, so the filter runs with sizes). With Sort By Size the arrival of the sizes reorders the folders and the filter runs again by itself.

verdicts.evidence:
Traced link by link, by reading; not run (no build allowed). src/finder/quick_look.rs:142-148: `let Some(finder) = self.finder.upgrade() else { return root; }; let root = root.on_action(text_size_handler::<PreviewTextBigger>(&finder, Some(1.)))` and two more, added before the `primary_entry` early return, so every frame has them. src/finder/preview.rs:706-712: `let view = view.clone(); move |_, window, cx| step_text_size(&view, steps, window, cx)`, a strong `Entity<Finder>` in a 'static closure. GPUI keeps that closure for as long as the frame is the window's: gpui-pre-0.3.10 src/elements/div.rs:3360-3362 `for (action_type, listener) in action_listeners { window.on_action(action_type, listener) }`; src/window.rs:6940-6942 `self.next_frame.dispatch_tree.on_action(action_type, Rc::new(listener))`; window.rs:3531-3532 `mem::swap(&mut self.rendered_frame, &mut self.next_frame); self.next_frame.clear();`. Only the old frame is cleared, and only after the new one is built, so a redraw upgrades the weak handle again while the old frame still holds the entity. An entity is released only at count zero (src/app/entity_map.rs:368-374), so `cx.observe_release_in(finder, window, |_, _, window, _| window.remove_window())` (quick_look.rs:44) cannot fire while that window lives.

Off macOS the app quits at the last window closed (gpui-pre src/app.rs:493-494; src/lib.rs:98-103), and Quick Look's window counts. verdicts.corrected_scenario: As the finder says. It holds for every way a browser goes while its Quick Look window is open: its tab closed (the tab's button, or Cmd+W with the keyboard in the browser's window; Quick Look's own window has no key for it), Move Tab to New Window, split view turned off, or the whole window closed. The browser lives exactly as long as that Quick Look window, so closing Quick Look (Space, Escape, its close button) releases it; this is not a leak for the life of the app. After the browser's whole window is gone, Quick Look's arrow keys do nothing and its Open button closes it without opening the file (`finder_window.update(..).ok()`, quick_look.rs:63-67 and 209-222). What would settle it at run time is the finder's test: second tab, Space on a file in the first, close the first tab, then expect Quick Look's window handle to be gone and a WeakEntity of the first tab's browser not to upgrade.

verdicts.corrected_scenario: Left: as the finder says, in the list view of a folder (tree mode is off in a search, Recents and the Trash), with the Preview Pane on (off by default) or with Quick Look open and the keyboard in the browser's window. It shows the spinner only when the parent's preview was never read: a folder that was selected before, as when it was opened with Right, has one cached and shows that, possibly out of date. The spinner goes at the next call of `selection_changed`: another selection, or a reread of the window's folder or of a folder open in the list.
